added_lemmas.statement: Let \(\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\) denote the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass.  The positive uniform path law and the causal use of the certified-calibration result are asserted only on this subclass and are not claimed over the full class studied by Fang--Ridder--Xie.  In the opposite direction, the fixed witness from \(\texttt{thm:no-uniform-atom-removed-modulus}\), with \(J=K=2\), \(p=(1/2,1/2)\), \(b=(64/65,1/65)\), \(\beta=1/65\), \(\mathcal H=[1,5/4]^2\), and \(\mathcal K_V=\{I_2\}\), satisfies the Fang--Ridder--Xie randomization, overlap, bounded-outcome, and positive-benchmark hypotheses.  Consequently the impossibility of a uniform atom-removed modulus transfers upward to that broader class: there is no function \(\widetilde A:(0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) with \(\widetilde A(x)\downarrow0\) that uniformly bounds \(P\{q<S(h,Z_V)\le q+x\}\) there.  Hence no uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion whose validity requires such a modulus is available over the broader class.  This negative transfer does not broaden either positive theorem, and the atom-safe one-sided conclusion of \(\mathsf A\) remains restricted to its declared inputs.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The class restriction for the positive statements follows directly from their quantifiers.  The conclusion of \(\texttt{thm:uniform-path-law}\) is uniform over
\[
 (P_n)_{n\geq 1}\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V),
\]
where \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) requires fixed finite \(J\) and \(K\), the finite-cell mass and treatment-overlap conditions, bounded potential outcomes, the local-remainder condition, benchmark positivity, and the covariance envelope.  The theorem contains no quantifier over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class.  The causal use of \(\texttt{thm:certified-calibration}\) is obtained by combining its Gaussian lower-CDF certificate with that path law, so this composition likewise supplies no positive conclusion outside \(\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\).

We next verify the direction in which class transfer is valid.  For the binary witness used by \(\texttt{thm:no-uniform-atom-removed-modulus}\), take \(X\) uniform on \(\{1,2\}\).  Conditional on \(X=j\), take \(A\) independent of the potential-outcome noises with
\[
 P(A=0\mid X=j)=P(A=1\mid X=j)=\frac12.
\]
Let \(\epsilon_0\) and \(\epsilon_1\) be independent symmetric random variables supported on \(\{-1/\sqrt8,1/\sqrt8\}\), and, conditional on \(X=j\), set
\[
 Y(0)=\epsilon_0,
 \qquad
 Y(1)=\frac{h_j}{\sqrt n}+\epsilon_1,
 \qquad
 Y=Y(A).
\]
Independent copies across units satisfy \(\texttt{ass:iid-rows}\).  The last equality is \(\texttt{ass:consistency}\), while the stipulated independence gives \(Y^{\mathrm{pot}}\perp A\mid X\), which is \(\texttt{ass:randomization}\).  Moreover,
\[
 p_j=\frac12,
 \qquad
 e_{ja}=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \mu_{n,j1}-\mu_{n,j0}=\frac{h_j}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Thus the stratum and treatment probabilities are bounded away from zero, and the local contrast remainder is exactly zero.  Since \(h_j\in[1,5/4]\),
\[
 \max_{a\in\{0,1\}}|Y(a)|
 \leq \frac54+\frac1{\sqrt8}<2,
\]
so the potential outcomes are uniformly bounded with \(B_Y=2\); likewise one may take \(p_{\min}=e_{\min}=1/2\).  The common benchmark \(b=(64/65,1/65)\) has
\[
 \min_{a\in\{0,1\}}b_a=\frac1{65}=\beta>0.
\]
These equations verify, one by one, randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive benchmark support, which are the Fang--Ridder--Xie hypotheses at issue.

For completeness, the contrast-score covariance also equals the covariance specified by the witness.  With action \(0\) as reference, the score in stratum \(j\) is
\[
 \xi_{n,j}
 =4\mathbf 1\{X=j\}
 \left[\mathbf 1\{A=1\}\epsilon_1-
       \mathbf 1\{A=0\}\epsilon_0\right].
\]
It has mean zero, and independence together with the displayed probabilities gives
\[
 E(\xi_{n,j}^2)
 =16\cdot\frac12
 \left(\frac12\cdot\frac18+\frac12\cdot\frac18\right)=1.
\]
For \(j\neq k\), \(\mathbf 1\{X=j\}\mathbf 1\{X=k\}=0\), hence \(E(\xi_{n,j}\xi_{n,k})=0\).  Therefore \(V_n=I_2\in\mathcal K_V\) upon taking \(v_{\min}=v_{\max}=1\).  This also verifies directly that the fixed witness is in the note's smaller model and, because it has the four published properties just checked, in the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class.

Now suppose, toward a contradiction, that the broader class admitted a uniform atom-removed modulus \(\widetilde A\) with \(\widetilde A(x)\downarrow0\).  Uniformity would apply after restriction to the preceding fixed binary design.  But \(\texttt{thm:no-uniform-atom-removed-modulus}\) supplies \(\eta>0\), \(h_m\in[1,5/4]^2\), \(q_m\in\mathbb R\), and \(x_m\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 P\{q_m<S(h_m,Z_{I_2})\leq q_m+x_m\}\geq\eta
 \qquad\text{for every }m.
\]
The asserted modulus would give
\[
 \eta
 \leq P\{q_m<S(h_m,Z_{I_2})\leq q_m+x_m\}
 \leq \widetilde A(x_m)
 \longrightarrow0,
\]
a contradiction.  Any class-uniform probability-to-critical-value argument based on such a modulus would, by its premise, provide exactly this forbidden uniform bound and therefore fails by the same restriction argument.  In contrast, \(\texttt{thm:certified-calibration}\) verifies a one-sided lower-CDF inequality at its returned rational critical value and explicitly permits atoms; it never converts probability error into a two-sided value width.  Its one-sided conclusion is therefore unaffected.  This proves the asymmetric transfer.
added_lemmas.justification: The class relation is asymmetric: the positive path law and calibration are proved only on the declared fixed finite-cell subclass, but a counterexample inside that subclass disproves any uniform atom-removed modulus on every broader class containing it.
added_lemmas.gap: Without an explicit transfer result, the fixed-cell witness could be misread as saying nothing about the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie setting, or the positive finite-cell theory could be misread as extending to that setting.
added_lemmas.consumer: Readers can use the positive theorem only under the declared finite-cell conditions, while implementers know that modulus-based two-sided critical-value conversion cannot be restored merely by moving to the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class.

proposed.comparator_claim: No uniform atom-removed modulus, and hence no modulus-based uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion, is available over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class because it contains the fixed binary collision witness.
A predetermined diverging inverse temperature yields root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity for the unsmoothed optimal-policy value.
Convergent binary treatment rules are represented by rules in a shifted Gaussian limit experiment.
A scalar empirical-process supremum is coupled nonasymptotically to the corresponding Gaussian supremum.
The concentration function of a standardized Gaussian-process supremum is bounded by its expected supremum.
Ordinary bootstrap consistency under a Gaussian limit is equivalent to full differentiability of the transformation.
Gaussian-vector maxima admit covariance comparison and anti-concentration bounds under arbitrary correlation.
A separation-of-variables transformation reduces Gaussian rectangle probabilities to bounded multiple integration.
Taylor expansion, interval analysis, and automatic differentiation self-validate Gaussian rectangle probabilities.
Recursive integration evaluates noncentered Gaussian orthant probabilities for positive-definite correlation matrices.
Joint Gaussian critical values give coverage after selecting a series dimension from the searched specification set.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparator table must record the asymmetric class result: no positive theorem is broadened, but the fixed binary impossibility witness transfers to the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite-stratum randomized lottery generates a continuum of benchmark-centered Gibbs rules indexed by a KL penalty. The normalized oracle-minus-estimated regret is compactified into one continuous path whose hard endpoint uses benchmark weights on every maximizing set and whose high-penalty endpoint is a projected categorical-covariance quadratic form. On the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass, the main positive result is a quantitative uniform Gaussian approximation for this nonlinear path, and an observed plug-in welfare frontier supplies an operational temperature selector. A finite interval-and-Gaussian-integration algorithm emits a machine-checkable one-sided certificate with an analytic fallback, so the simultaneous envelope remains valid after every observed-data-measurable temperature choice and at quantile atoms. These positive results are not claimed over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. Conversely, a legal fixed binary collision witness lies in that broader class, so the failure of uniform atom-removed anti-concentration, and of every modulus-based uniform probability-to-critical-value conversion, transfers upward.

project_justification.gap: Fixed positive KL penalties have a quadratic regret law, while hard assignment boundaries and softmax inference for predetermined smoothing sequences are studied separately. No published result supplies a quantitative joint path law or a certified one-sided critical value over the full penalty menu on the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass. Standard Gaussian-supremum anti-concentration also does not cover the hard-cell atom collisions exhibited here; because the binary witness satisfies the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie hypotheses, enlarging to that class cannot recover a uniform atom-removed modulus.
project_justification.niche: Finite multiaction lotteries create a tractable but nonstandard function-valued statistic: interior coordinates are nonlinear Gaussian transforms, the hard endpoint is directionally irregular with benchmark-weighted multiway ties, and the opposite endpoint has a different quadratic normalization. The fixed finite-cell structure supports the positive approximation and certified computation. The same structure contains a binary atom-collision witness, which is enough for an upward negative transfer even though positive achievability does not transfer upward.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the primitive finite-cell Gaussian certificate, matches both endpoints, proves an explicit tie-slab coupling rate in \(C([0,1])\), defines a sample-computable plug-in frontier and its observed-data sigma-field, and turns a verified lower CDF bracket with directed rounding and a finite fallback into computably honest inference after temperature choice. It also proves the hard-cell atom formula, constructs a fixed legal counterexample to uniform atom-removed anti-concentration, and proves the asymmetric class-transfer corollary: positive results remain on the finite-cell subclass, whereas the impossibility and every modulus-based critical-value obstruction extend to the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class.

prose_updates.related_work: Fang--Ridder--Xie studies benchmark-centered KL assignment and proves a quadratic regret limit for each fixed positive penalty; its Conclusion leaves data-driven penalty choice open, and its deterministic binary analysis is separate. The positive path law and certified calibration here are restricted to the declared fixed finite-cell randomized subclass and are not asserted over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. The relation reverses for the negative result: the fixed two-stratum binary collision design satisfies their randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, so a uniform atom-removed modulus or any modulus-based probability-to-critical-value conversion over their broader class would contradict the witness theorem. Their three-arm commitment-savings frontier motivates an illustration, not a finite-stratification adequacy claim. Whitehouse--Chen--Austern--Syrgkanis uses softmax smoothing for one unsmoothed optimal-policy value along a predetermined diverging temperature, a different scalar target. Hirano--Porter supplies the shifted-Gaussian local decision experiment for binary hard treatment choice, not a multiaction path law. Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato and Giessing give anti-concentration for Gaussian-process suprema, whereas \(G(h,Z_V)\) is nonlinear and has the proved hard-cell atom collisions. Fang--Santos explains directional irregularity but does not furnish atom-safe continuum calibration. Genz, Wang--Kennedy, and Miwa--Hayter--Kuriki provide Gaussian integration components, not certification of this nonlinear continuum event. Kang supplies simultaneous-band selection logic for an observed series path; the present bridge additionally separates the observed selector frontier from the unobserved oracle causal-regret target.
prose_updates.interpretation: The positive output is deliberately one-sided and subclass-specific: for the declared fixed finite-cell randomized model, it certifies that the entire normalized oracle-regret path lies below one auditable critical value, so any temperature selected measurably from observed data inherits the same guarantee. No such positive path law or causal calibration claim is made for the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. The negative conclusion does extend: nearby local states in a fixed binary design belonging to that broader class place positive hard-cell atoms arbitrarily close together. Thus moving to the broader class cannot create a uniform atom-removed modulus or a modulus-based uniform conversion from probability error to critical-value error.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The one-sided algorithm terminates and certifies coverage on its declared finite-cell inputs because work-capped refinement has an analytic Gaussian-tail fallback. It need not return a critical value within a prescribed numerical distance of \(Q_{1-\alpha}^{\mathrm{LF}}\). The fixed two-stratum binary witness shows that no uniform atom-removed modulus follows even over the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class: distinct positive hard-cell atoms can collide while retaining positive mass. Thus a modulus-based two-sided value-width certificate would need additional atom separation, a restricted local-state set, or another explicit structural condition. This is an upward transfer only for the obstruction; it does not broaden the positive approximation or calibration theorem. The rational fallback \(2B_\gamma^++(B_\gamma^+)^2/2\) can be conservative.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The positive path-law and causal calibration results are uniform only for fixed \(J\) and \(K\), positive benchmark probabilities, positive stratum and treatment probabilities, bounded outcomes, compact local contrasts, and covariance spectra bounded away from zero. They exclude boundary benchmarks, singular covariance, growing action or stratum counts, disappearing cells, and continuous covariates without a prespecified finite stratification. They are not claimed over the full Fang--Ridder--Xie class. The commitment-savings display is an illustration conditional on prespecified cells. Temperature selection is restricted to \(\mathcal F_n^{\mathrm{obs}}\)-measurable rules, including rules based on the displayed plug-in frontier; that frontier is not claimed to estimate the unobserved oracle regret path. The negative scope is broader: the fixed binary witness already satisfies the Fang--Ridder--Xie randomization, overlap, boundedness, and positive-benchmark hypotheses, so the no-modulus result and every modulus-based probability-to-critical-value obstruction transfer upward. No non-modulus impossibility theorem is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: The corollary makes the class relation exact: positive achievability remains on the fixed finite-cell randomized subclass, whereas a counterexample in that subclass transfers the impossibility to every broader class containing it.
statement_notes.gap: The witness theorem alone does not state how its negative conclusion compares with the broader Fang--Ridder--Xie class, and broadening a negative result must not be confused with broadening the positive path law.
statement_notes.consumer: Readers and implementers can distinguish the finite-cell domain of the certified procedure from the broader domain on which modulus-based two-sided critical-value conversion is impossible.
